qr.prompt: I take it you weren't thrilled with the proposal.
qr.promptKo: 제안이 그다지 마음에 들지 않으셨나 보네요.

options.text: Not exactly. It raised more questions than it answered.
options.ko: 그렇죠. 답보다 질문이 더 많이 생겼어요.

options.text: I'll take it with me.
The proposal was on Tuesday.

options.text: I pushed the door open.
It's worth asking, but I doubt it.

options.text: The launch was last week.

It starts later than usual.

options.text: The loop is two kilometers.
Might be wise, given the contract terms.

options.text: They played well, didn't they?

options.text: Someone double-counted the March invoices.
They came up yesterday.
Add them to the list.

qr.promptKo: 사라 소식 들을 때까지 답장은 보류하는 게 좋겠어요.

options.text: She'll hold the event in May.
Off the top of my head, two.
Fair enough. I'll sit on the draft for now.

qr.prompt: Wouldn't it be cheaper to outsource it?
qr.promptKo: 외주를 주는 게 더 싸지 않을까요?

options.text: It's cheaper at the outlet store.
In the short run, maybe, but we'd lose control over quality.
options.ko: 단기적으로는 그럴지 몰라도 품질 관리를 못 하게 돼요.

options.text: It's just outside the building.

qr.prompt: Who's going to break the news to the team?
qr.promptKo: 팀에 그 소식은 누가 전할 건가요?

options.text: I suppose it falls to me.
The news was on at nine.
It broke during shipping.

qr.prompt: This report could use another pair of eyes.
qr.promptKo: 이 보고서는 누가 한 번 더 봐 주면 좋겠어요.

options.text: My eyes are tired.
I could take a look this afternoon.
options.ko: 오늘 오후에 제가 볼 수 있어요.

options.text: It's a nice pair of glasses.

qr.prompt: What if enterprise sales take longer than you expect?
qr.promptKo: 기업 영업이 예상보다 오래 걸리면 어떡하죠?

options.text: Sales were up last quarter.
I expect so, yes.
Then we fall back on the consumer side while we adjust.
options.ko: 그럼 조정하는 동안 소비자 쪽에 의지하면 돼요.

qr.prompt: Is something going on that I should know about?

options.text: Actually, yes. Things have been difficult at home.
options.ko: 사실 네. 집에 좀 힘든 일이 있어요.

options.text: It's going on Tuesday.
I know about it already.

options.text: I finally got the offer.
Then I'm afraid we may need to walk away.
options.ko: 그럼 유감이지만 협상을 접어야 할 것 같아요.

options.text: Forty is a good age.

qr.prompt: Couldn't the causation run the other way?
qr.promptKo: 인과 관계가 반대일 수도 있지 않나요?

options.text: I'd rather run in the morning.
The other way is closed.
It could, which is why we're running a follow-up study.
options.ko: 그럴 수 있어요. 그래서 후속 연구를 하고 있어요.

qr.prompt: Can I ask what tipped the balance?

options.text: Mainly the chance to lead my own team.
The balance is in my account.
I'll leave a tip on the table.

qr.prompt: Isn't your sample far too small?

options.text: Small, medium, or large?
It is limited, which is why I called the results preliminary.
The samples are free.

qr.prompt: Was it worth the hype?

options.text: It's worth about fifty dollars.
I hyped it up a lot.
Partly. The view was, the food wasn't.

qr.prompt: If you really want it, I'd bid higher.

options.text: We set our limit for a reason.
It's higher than the building.
I bid you good night.

qr.prompt: Well, it's certainly a brave idea.

options.text: Thanks, I'm not scared of anything.
Do you see any risks I might have missed?
Bravery runs in my family.

qr.prompt: I feel like you're not listening to me anymore.
qr.promptKo: 네가 더 이상 내 말을 안 듣는 것 같아.

options.text: I'm listening to a podcast.
I can't hear the music.
I'm sorry it feels that way. Help me understand.
options.ko: 그렇게 느꼈다니 미안해. 이해할 수 있게 말해 줘.

qr.prompt: Why should customers trust you after this?
qr.promptKo: 이 일 이후 고객이 왜 당신들을 믿어야 하죠?

options.text: They shouldn't just take our word. Judge us by what we do next.
options.ko: 말만 믿으시면 안 돼요. 앞으로의 행동으로 판단해 주세요.

options.text: Our customers are mostly young.
Trust me, it's delicious.

qr.prompt: Are there going to be more cuts?

options.text: I cut my finger yesterday.
None are planned, and I'll tell you the moment that changes.
options.ko: 계획된 건 없고, 바뀌면 바로 알려 드릴게요.

options.text: Short cuts are faster.

qr.prompt: I need the redesign live by Friday.

options.text: I live near the office.
Friday is my favorite day.
We can, if we pause the mobile work for two weeks.

qr.prompt: Would you like to say a few words?

options.text: Just briefly. Thank you for everything, Maria.
I know a few words in French.
The words are on the screen.

lines.text: So, where do we stand with the supplier negotiations?
lines.ko: 그래서 공급업체 협상은 어디까지 왔어요?

lines.text: They've agreed to the volume discount, but they're refusing to budge on delivery times.
lines.ko: 대량 할인은 동의했는데 납기는 꿈쩍도 안 해요.

lines.text: Then we need a fallback. What if we split orders between them and the Busan supplier?
lines.ko: 그럼 대안이 필요하네요. 그쪽이랑 부산 업체에 주문을 나누면 어때요?

lines.text: It would cost more upfront, but it'd hedge against delays. I'll run the numbers.
lines.ko: 초기 비용은 더 들겠지만 지연 위험은 줄겠네요. 계산해 볼게요.

lines.text: Do that, and let's revisit it on Friday before we commit.
lines.ko: 그렇게 해 주시고, 확정하기 전에 금요일에 다시 봐요.

questions.q: What has the supplier agreed to?
What does the woman propose?
What is the drawback of the plan?

lines.text: I read your draft. The findings are interesting, but the sample size seems awfully small to draw such firm conclusions.
lines.ko: 초안 읽었어요. 결과는 흥미롭지만 그렇게 단정적인 결론을 내리기엔 표본이 너무 작아 보여요.

lines.text: That's fair. We only had sixty participants because the funding was cut midway.
lines.ko: 맞는 말이에요. 중간에 예산이 깎여서 참가자가 60명뿐이었어요.

lines.text: Then I'd soften the language. Present it as a pilot study and propose a larger follow-up.
lines.ko: 그럼 표현을 누그러뜨리세요. 예비 연구로 제시하고 더 큰 후속 연구를 제안하는 거죠.

lines.text: Good point. It might even strengthen our next grant application.
lines.ko: 좋은 지적이에요. 다음 연구비 신청에 오히려 도움이 될 수도 있겠네요.

questions.q: What concern does the woman raise?
Why were there few participants?
What does the man think of the suggestion?
options: It could help a future grant application.

lines.text: Can I be frank? The design team feels like they're being blamed for delays that started upstream.
lines.ko: 솔직하게 말해도 될까요? 디자인팀은 앞 단계에서 시작된 지연 때문에 비난받는다고 느껴요.

lines.text: I wasn't aware it was coming across that way. The deadlines were set before the requirements changed.
lines.ko: 그렇게 비치는 줄 몰랐어요. 마감은 요구사항이 바뀌기 전에 정해졌거든요.

lines.text: Exactly. Maybe a joint retrospective would clear the air?
lines.ko: 바로 그거예요. 합동 회고를 하면 분위기가 풀리지 않을까요?

lines.text: Agreed. Let's keep it blame-free and focus on the handoff process.
lines.ko: 동의해요. 누구 탓도 하지 말고 인수인계 과정에 집중하죠.

questions.q: How does the design team feel?
According to the man, why were there delays?
options: Requirements changed after deadlines were set.

questions.q: What will they do next?

lines.text: Most of us assume that multitasking makes us more productive. The research, however, tells a rather different story.
lines.ko: 우리 대부분은 멀티태스킹이 생산성을 높인다고 생각합니다. 하지만 연구 결과는 꽤 다른 이야기를 합니다.

lines.text: When we switch between tasks, we lose time re-orienting ourselves, and those small losses add up to as much as a third of our working day.
lines.ko: 일을 오갈 때마다 다시 집중하느라 시간을 잃고, 그 작은 손실이 쌓이면 근무 시간의 3분의 1에 이릅니다.

lines.text: Today I'll argue that the most productive people aren't doing more at once. They're simply better at protecting their attention.
lines.ko: 오늘 저는 가장 생산적인 사람들이 한꺼번에 더 많이 하는 게 아니라 주의력을 더 잘 지킬 뿐이라고 말씀드리겠습니다.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the talk?
How much of the working day can be lost?
questions.qKo: 근무 시간 중 얼마나 잃을 수 있나요?

questions.q: What will the speaker argue?

lines.text: Revenue for the third quarter came in slightly below forecast, largely because of weaker demand in Europe.
lines.ko: 3분기 매출은 주로 유럽 수요 부진으로 전망치를 약간 밑돌았습니다.

lines.text: That said, our subscription business grew by eighteen percent, and customer retention is at a record high.
lines.ko: 그렇긴 해도 구독 사업은 18% 성장했고 고객 유지율은 사상 최고입니다.

lines.text: Going forward, we'll be shifting marketing spend away from hardware and toward subscriptions.
lines.ko: 앞으로는 마케팅 비용을 하드웨어에서 구독 쪽으로 옮길 예정입니다.

questions.q: Why was revenue below forecast?
What grew by eighteen percent?
What will the company change?

lines.text: For centuries, the town's economy depended entirely on the river. Fishing, trade, even the local festivals revolved around it.
lines.ko: 수 세기 동안 이 마을의 경제는 전적으로 강에 의존했습니다. 어업, 교역, 심지어 지역 축제까지 강을 중심으로 돌아갔죠.

lines.text: But when a dam was built upstream in the nineteen seventies, the fish disappeared almost overnight.
lines.ko: 하지만 1970년대 상류에 댐이 들어서자 물고기가 거의 하룻밤 사이에 사라졌습니다.

lines.text: What followed was a slow, painful reinvention, one that would eventually turn this quiet fishing town into a center for renewable energy research.
lines.ko: 그 뒤로 느리고 고통스러운 변신이 이어졌고, 결국 이 조용한 어촌은 재생에너지 연구의 중심지가 되었습니다.

questions.q: What did the town's economy depend on?
What caused the fish to disappear?
What is the town known for now?

lines.text: The overheating video has spread to the national news, and our share price dropped six percent this morning.
lines.ko: 과열 영상이 전국 뉴스로 퍼졌고 오늘 아침 주가가 6퍼센트 떨어졌어요.

lines.text: Legal still wants us to wait for the lab results, which won't be ready until Thursday.
lines.ko: 법무팀은 여전히 목요일에나 나오는 실험 결과를 기다리자고 해요.

lines.text: Three days of silence would be far more damaging than admitting we don't have all the answers yet.
lines.ko: 사흘 침묵은 아직 답을 다 모른다고 인정하는 것보다 훨씬 더 큰 타격이에요.

lines.text: Agreed. Let's pause sales, offer refunds immediately, and have the CEO speak on camera this afternoon.
lines.ko: 동의해요. 판매를 멈추고 즉시 환불을 제안하고 오늘 오후 CEO가 카메라 앞에서 말하게 하죠.

questions.q: What happened to the share price?
Why does the legal team want to wait?
What will the CEO do?

lines.text: Our platform delivers roughly seventy percent of the traffic, so a sixty-forty split seems more than fair to us.
lines.ko: 저희 플랫폼이 트래픽의 약 70퍼센트를 가져오니 6대 4는 충분히 공정해 보여요.

lines.text: Traffic is one thing, but our content drives the subscriptions, and that's where the real revenue is.
lines.ko: 트래픽도 중요하지만 구독을 이끄는 건 저희 콘텐츠고, 진짜 매출은 거기서 나와요.

lines.text: What if we started at fifty-five forty-five and revisited it after twelve months of data?
lines.ko: 55대 45로 시작해서 12개월 데이터를 보고 다시 논의하면 어떨까요?

lines.text: That could work, as long as the metrics for the review are defined in the contract now.
lines.ko: 검토 지표를 지금 계약서에 명시한다면 가능하겠네요.

questions.q: How much traffic does the first company bring?
What does the second speaker say drives revenue?
questions.qKo: 두 번째 화자가 말한 매출의 원천은?

questions.q: What condition is set for the compromise?

lines.text: I've deducted six hundred from your deposit for the scratches on the wooden floor.
lines.ko: 나무 바닥 긁힘 때문에 보증금에서 600을 공제했어요.

lines.text: Those scratches were there when I moved in. I listed them on the inspection form you signed.
lines.ko: 그 긁힘은 입주할 때부터 있었어요. 서명하신 점검표에 적어 뒀어요.

lines.text: I don't have a copy of that form anymore.
lines.ko: 그 점검표 사본이 이제 없어요.

lines.text: I do, and I'll email it today. If the deduction isn't reversed within two weeks, I'll take it to the tenancy board.
lines.ko: 저한테 있어요, 오늘 메일로 보낼게요. 2주 안에 공제가 취소되지 않으면 임대차 위원회에 가져갈게요.

questions.q: Why did the landlord deduct money?
What evidence does the tenant have?
What will the tenant do if nothing changes?

lines.text: I've been offered a director role, but it means managing twenty people and almost no hands-on design work.
lines.ko: 디렉터 자리를 제안받았는데 20명을 관리하고 실무 디자인은 거의 못 하게 돼요.

lines.text: What part of your current job gives you the most energy? Be honest with yourself.
lines.ko: 지금 일에서 어떤 부분이 가장 힘이 나요? 스스로에게 솔직해 봐요.

lines.text: Honestly, the moments when I solve a tricky design problem on my own.
lines.ko: 솔직히 까다로운 디자인 문제를 혼자 풀 때요.

lines.text: Then ask whether there's a principal designer track. Plenty of companies pay senior experts as much as directors.
lines.ko: 그럼 수석 디자이너 트랙이 있는지 물어봐요. 시니어 전문가에게 디렉터만큼 주는 회사가 많아요.

questions.q: What does the new role involve?
What gives the speaker the most energy?
What does the mentor suggest?

lines.text: There are five offers on the house, and the seller wants to decide by Monday evening.
lines.ko: 그 집에 제안이 다섯 건이고 매도인은 월요일 저녁까지 결정하고 싶어 해요.

lines.text: We really can't go above our budget. Is there anything else that might give us an edge?
lines.ko: 예산을 넘길 순 없어요. 유리하게 만들 다른 방법이 있을까요?

lines.text: The seller is moving overseas, so a fast, simple closing could matter more to her than a slightly higher price.
lines.ko: 매도인이 해외로 이주해서 조금 높은 가격보다 빠르고 간단한 잔금이 더 중요할 수 있어요.

lines.text: Then let's offer to close in three weeks and drop our request for her to repaint the bedrooms.
lines.ko: 그럼 3주 내 잔금을 제안하고 침실 재도색 요청은 빼죠.

questions.q: How many offers are there?
Why might a fast closing matter to the seller?
options: She needs money for a business.

questions.q: What will the buyers drop from their offer?

lines.text: Ten years ago, we believed that more data would automatically lead to better decisions. It didn't.
lines.ko: 10년 전 우리는 데이터가 많을수록 결정이 자동으로 나아진다고 믿었습니다. 그렇지 않았죠.

lines.text: What we learned is that data without a clear question simply creates more noise and more meetings.
lines.ko: 우리가 배운 건, 명확한 질문 없는 데이터는 소음과 회의만 늘린다는 것입니다.

lines.text: So my challenge to you this year is simple: before you build another dashboard, write down the decision it's meant to support.
lines.ko: 올해 제 제안은 간단합니다. 대시보드를 또 만들기 전에, 그것이 도울 결정을 먼저 적어 보세요.

questions.q: What did people believe ten years ago?
What does data without a clear question create?
questions.qKo: 명확한 질문 없는 데이터가 만드는 것은?

questions.q: What is the speaker's challenge?
options: Write down the decision before building a dashboard

lines.text: I want to address last month's decision on bonuses directly, because many of you told me it felt imposed rather than discussed.
lines.ko: 지난달 보너스 결정에 대해 직접 말씀드리고 싶습니다. 많은 분이 논의가 아니라 강요로 느꼈다고 하셨죠.

lines.text: You were right. For this year, we're returning to the previous structure, effective immediately.
lines.ko: 여러분이 옳았습니다. 올해는 즉시 이전 체계로 돌아갑니다.

lines.text: Next year's plan will be designed by a working group with one representative from every department.
lines.ko: 내년 계획은 모든 부서 대표 한 명씩으로 구성된 실무 그룹이 설계합니다.

questions.q: How did employees feel about the decision?
What happens this year?
Who will design next year's plan?
options: A group with a representative from every department

lines.text: Our study followed twelve hundred teenagers for three years and measured both screen time and reported anxiety.
lines.ko: 저희 연구는 청소년 1,200명을 3년간 추적하며 화면 시간과 보고된 불안을 모두 측정했습니다.

lines.text: Contrary to many headlines, total screen time predicted very little. What mattered was late-night use that cut into sleep.
lines.ko: 많은 헤드라인과 달리 총 화면 시간은 거의 예측력이 없었습니다. 중요한 건 수면을 갉아먹는 심야 사용이었습니다.

lines.text: Our recommendation, therefore, is not to ban phones but to keep them out of bedrooms after ten.
lines.ko: 따라서 저희 권고는 휴대폰 금지가 아니라 10시 이후 침실에 두지 않는 것입니다.

questions.q: How long did the study last?
What mattered most for anxiety?
options: Late-night use that cut into sleep

questions.q: What do the researchers recommend?
options: Keeping phones out of bedrooms after ten

lines.text: In thirty-one years here, Daniel trained more of us than anyone can count, and he never once took credit for our success.
lines.ko: 31년 동안 다니엘은 셀 수 없이 많은 우리를 가르쳤고, 우리의 성공을 한 번도 자기 공으로 돌리지 않았습니다.

lines.text: He used to say that a good manager makes the team look brilliant and himself look unnecessary.
lines.ko: 그는 좋은 관리자는 팀을 빛나게 하고 자신은 필요 없어 보이게 만든다고 말하곤 했죠.

lines.text: Daniel, you were never unnecessary. Please raise your glasses to a well-earned retirement.
lines.ko: 다니엘, 당신은 결코 필요 없는 사람이 아니었어요. 마땅히 누릴 은퇴를 위해 잔을 들어 주세요.

questions.q: How long did Daniel work there?
What did Daniel never do?
questions.qKo: 다니엘이 한 번도 하지 않은 것은?
options: Take credit for the team's success

questions.q: What does the speaker ask everyone to do?

lines.text: To sum up today's discussion, our panelists agreed that individual action and regulation are not rivals but partners.
lines.ko: 오늘 토론을 정리하면, 패널들은 개인의 행동과 규제가 경쟁자가 아니라 동반자라는 데 동의했습니다.

lines.text: Where they disagreed was on speed: some argued for gradual change to protect jobs, others for urgent bans.
lines.ko: 의견이 갈린 건 속도였습니다. 일부는 일자리를 지키기 위한 점진적 변화를, 다른 이들은 시급한 금지를 주장했죠.

lines.text: The full recording will be online tomorrow, along with the reports each panelist mentioned.
lines.ko: 전체 녹화본은 각 패널이 언급한 보고서와 함께 내일 온라인에 올라갑니다.
